claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within Pulumi and is never sent to the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own, separate deletion-protection attributes, which the cloud provider enforces independently of anything Pulumi knows about.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute (deletion protection enforced by the cloud provider).
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute (deletion protection enforced by the cloud provider).
A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi and still refuse to delete due to provider-side deletion protection, or be protected in Pulumi while the provider-side deletion protection is off (vice versa).

The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi protect and provider deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes, separate from Pulumi's `protect` resource option, which the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi.
`deletionProtection` is a deletion-protection attribute on a GCP Cloud SQL instance in the Pulumi GCP provider.
`deletionProtection` is a deletion-protection attribute on an AWS RDS instance in the Pulumi AWS provider.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and a cloud resource's own deletion-protection attributes are complementary rather than substitutes for one another.

The docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi protect and resource-level deletion protection apart and resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
Pulumi has no single flag to protect every resource in a stack; stack transforms can be used to set `protect: true` on every resource as it is registered.
The docs page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/transforms/ has a 'stack-transforms' section.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When `pulumi destroy` fails on a protected resource, the error message names a URN and mentions `protect`.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove the `protect` option.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, and the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the Pulumi provider.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the Pulumi provider.
Some clouds reject the delete call themselves, independent of Pulumi; the error text comes back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked`.
AWS RDS `deletionProtection` is enforced by the AWS API.
EC2 `disableApiTermination` is enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
An Azure Resource Manager management lock causes delete calls to be rejected by Azure, with error code `ScopeLocked`.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently says, so setting the attribute to `false` in the program alone is not enough.

To remove deletion protection set by a provider or cloud API: set the attribute to `false` in the Pulumi program, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches both the live resource and Pulumi state, then run `pulumi destroy`.

If deletion protection was already disabled outside Pulumi (e.g., in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes stack state with reality and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the Pulumi provider.
`gcp.bigquery.Dataset` has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute; destroying a dataset that still contains tables fails unless it is `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` has a `forceDestroy` attribute that defaults to `false`; a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute.
`aws.dynamodb.Table` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist in the Pulumi azure-native provider.
An Azure `CanNotDelete` management lock, enforced by Azure Resource Manager, must be removed before the resource can be deleted, independent of the Pulumi program.
Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it; recreating a vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Azure Key Vault purge protection prevents purging a soft-deleted vault until its retention period elapses.
